text:
Los Angeles played the game that usually wins and lost it anyway. LAK carried 2.92 expected goals to BOS's 2.12, and in a simulated replay of every shot the Kings win 66 percent of the time. The scoreboard said BOS 4, LAK 1, and the difference was Jeremy Swayman. He stopped 25 of 26 shots against 2.92 expected goals, saving 1.92 goals more than the chances deserved, while Anton Forsberg at the other end stopped 24 of 26, almost exactly what his chances called for.

The Kings made their case early. Alex Laferriere scored 31 seconds in, a wrist shot set up by Adrian Kempe and Brandt Clarke, and LAK outchanced BOS 1.29 to 0.39 in expected goals over the first period. Scott Laughton had a 28 percent look that Swayman turned away. The game then flattened out. The second period was nearly even, and David Pastrnak tied it at 2:43 with a snap shot that carried only a 3 percent chance of going in.

The third period belonged to the Bruins, who scored three times in the final 6:24. Marat Khusnutdinov put them ahead at 13:36 with a backhand, Elias Lindholm made it 3-1 at 18:02, and JJ Peterka sealed it at 19:42 with a wrist shot, Pastrnak assisting. Two of those goals came on 5 percent chances. Neither team scored on the power play, 0 for 2 each, and BOS's 24 giveaways to LAK's 11 suggest the Bruins were not the cleaner side. They were just the one that finished.
